name: footprint
description: Maps an organisation's external footprint from its own traffic: the contact details it publishes (emails, telephone numbers, postal addresses), the social-media accounts and source-code repositories it links to, the cloud storage buckets, package-registry entries and third-party services it uses, and the API and documentation endpoints it exposes. Each is recorded as a finding. Social and source links are judged by where they sit — an account in the header or footer (or carrying rel="me") is the organisation's own; one in the page content may be a third party's. It only reads responses: nothing is held, changed or sent.

settings.label: Detectors to skip
settings.description: Detector ids (email, phone, github, bucket, ga4, …) or whole categories (contact, social-account, source-repo, cloud-storage, package, service-id, api-endpoint) never to report. The README lists every id.

settings.label: Include links to individual posts and files
settings.description: Off: only accounts and repositories (a social profile, an org or repo page) are recorded. On: links to individual posts, videos and repository files are recorded too, which is far noisier.

settings.label: Most findings from one response
settings.description: A page that links out dozens of times is stopped at the cap.

settings.label: Largest body scanned (KiB)
settings.description: Bodies bigger than this are left alone. Links are extracted in Go and the service-identifier patterns are anchored on a literal, so most of the scan is cheap at any size.

settings.label: Largest body scanned for emails and phone numbers (KiB)
settings.description: An email address or a telephone number has no fixed text to search for first, so those patterns read the body itself. This keeps that bounded; every other detector still covers the whole body.
